Maya Patel: Heads up — hit a case where the eval-harness CI produced unredacted prompt artifacts for a private customer benchmark during a quantization run. Not public data but still sensitive. Repro below, marking as P0 until we confirm scope.

Raj Singh: Yikes. Can you paste the repro + where the artifacts landed?

Maya Patel: repro steps:
1) checkout feature/quantize-bench
2) ./scripts/run_eval.sh --config ci/quantize-bench.yaml --save-artifacts=on --redact=off --model redwood/llama-3b-q4
3) artifacts: s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/ci/2026-06-11/1795004321/
logs had a chunk of the original customer prompt in plain text under artifacts/input_prompts.json

Sylvie Chen: Can you paste a sanitized excerpt? We need to assess whether it's just a prompt template or contains PII.

Maya Patel: pasted sanitized excerpt (replacing real tokens with [REDACTED]):
```
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "prompt": "Please summarize the following user email: [REDACTED_PERSON_NAME] wrote: \"I transferred $5,000 to account 123-456-789...\"",
  "meta": {"customer_id": "cust_42"}
}
```

Anika Torres: That looks like customer-sensitive content (partial PII). Immediate steps: 1) flip CI default to --redact=on, 2) add artifact ACL/retention lock so artifacts are not world-readable, 3) add a test that fails if any artifact contains common PII patterns. I can open PRs for 1+2.

Tom Wright: For the PII check, add a lightweight regex scan in the harness pre-upload hook. Example pytest snippet we can add to ci/tests/test_artifact_safety.py:
```
def test_no_plain_pii(tmp_path):
    artifacts = gather_artifacts(tmp_path)
    assert not contains_ssn_like(artifacts)
```
We'll also log matches to a secure audit queue rather than to stdout.

Raj Singh: We should also ensure the S3 upload uses customer-isolated prefixes with bucket policy that denies s3:GetObject unless the caller is in the eval-ci-service role. I'll own the infra change.

Maya Patel: Thanks. One more thing — the redaction library we use (redactlib v0.9) misses numeric-account-like patterns in some tokenized outputs after quantization. Could be related to tokenization/bytepair splitting. We need a short experiment: run the same eval with quantized model but with post-token-join scan to catch reassembled PII.

Sylvie Chen: Filed an issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/ML-ev-893. Suggested labels: security, ci, eval-harness.

eval-ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered: build/quantize-bench #278 failed on step upload-artifacts (exit code 0 -> artifacts contain matches). See https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/278 for logs.

Anika Torres: I'll open PR to change default flags and add S3 ACLs: PR #4327. Also adding retention/purge job to remove artifacts older than 7 days unless explicitly flagged for debugging.

Tom Wright: I'll add the pytest PII guard and a small fuzz test that reconstructs token joins to catch the quantization edge-case. PR #4330.

Raj Singh: Infra PR for bucket policy and KMS key rotation is coming this afternoon. I'll also add role binding so only eval-ci-service and compliance-team can read artifacts.

Maya Patel: Assigning myself to run a full scan across last 30 days' artifacts to estimate blast radius. Will post results here when done. Thanks all. :eyes:

Sylvie Chen: Good call. Also add a CI gating rule: any artifact upload step failing the PII scan should fail the job and trigger an incident runbook.

Maya Patel: Agreed — runbook note: rotate customer/artifact keys if we discover exposed PII and contact SecOps.

Raj Singh: ack, taking ownership for the infra pieces.

Anika Torres: merging PRs once reviews complete, will ping here. :thumbsup:

Maya Patel: Closing loop — created followup checklist in the issue: change default redact, add artifact ACLs, add PII tests, run scan of past artifacts, purge policy, runbook update.

Tom Wright: +1

eval-ci-bot: Reminder: deploy scheduled for 2026-06-11T18:00Z (auto-rollout).
